findings.title: Hierarchy became a durable rule

The retained screenshot review identifies the images as last-escape frames at move 17 of a 27-move Renju game. Their exact browser, runtime build, capture date, DPR and physical-device conditions were not recorded.
The images document static presentation in 0.4.6 and 0.4.7. The 0.4.8 release notes document the following mistake-analysis work; these images are not labelled as 0.4.8 captures.
human: The original review text and its four active-frame images supply the design evidence. This case was assembled later; original-period human approval is not established by the preserved file.
followUp: The original review left marker legibility and the amount of mobile explanation under review. The 0.4.8 source notes extend this sequence; no original-period active-frame image for that release was recovered.

process.title: Make presentation a product responsibility
process.detail: The 0.5 plan treated the reports as useful product surfaces. Rust continued to emit structured evidence; the web app took responsibility for navigation, tables and detail views. The two report destinations became one Lab.

process.title: Use the same visual language
process.detail: Visuals replaced the separate asset-preview pages with a React view for sprites, icons, colours and typography. Shared controls and navigation connected the reference material to the game it explained.

process.title: Keep player explanations focused
process.detail: Rules and Guide added an explanation layer inside the app. Concrete examples and board diagrams helped explain rules, markers and replay analysis. Players could use that reference alongside the deeper project documents.

findings.title: Generated data and authored presentation had different owners
findings.detail: Compact report data remained inspectable without carrying a second generated website alongside the application.

findings.title: The supporting pages needed the same care as the board
findings.detail: Navigation, typography and spacing could make Lab and Visuals feel part of Gomoku2D while preserving their distinct jobs.

technical: The existing qualified history captures are reused without changing their pixels. Their source paths, SHA-256, PNG dimensions and exact tagged sources remain recorded.
History builds used modern toolchains and Chromium with synthetic state, UTC/en-US and reduced motion. These are reconstructed release layouts, not original release binaries or physical-phone checks.
human: The release plan records the intended ownership and product direction. This assembled review uses later qualified captures of the tagged pages; original-period human approval is not established here.
followUp: The 0.6.3 developer area builds on this shared shell with source-backed asset inspection and reusable review tools.

title: Sharing through the replay sidebar
question: How could sharing feel like a replay action while leaving enough room for its controls?
summary: Share replay takes over the existing sidebar. Publish follows the same pattern, with distinct icons, a compact preview and the same route back to playback.

process.title: Give sharing the whole control area
process.detail: An expansion below the replay controls made the bottom of the sidebar crowded. Replacing the sidebar gave the preview, player labels and share action a clear place. Opening the pane pauses playback; closing it returns to the replay controls.

process.title: Apply the pattern to publishing
process.detail: Publish replay initially introduced another expansion. It was brought into the same full-sidebar interaction. A separate Publish icon makes its public-profile role distinct from sharing a self-contained link.

findings.title: A repeated interaction reduced new UI
findings.detail: Share and Publish use the same pane transition, close control and preview structure. Their different destinations remain explicit.

findings.title: The action needed to belong to the game
findings.detail: Compact preview content, authored icons and the existing control styles replaced the feel of a generic web form attached below Replay.

technical: The existing qualified history captures are reused without changing their pixels. Their source paths, SHA-256, PNG dimensions and exact tagged sources remain recorded.
History builds used modern toolchains and Chromium with synthetic state, UTC/en-US and reduced motion. These are reconstructed release layouts, not original release binaries or physical-phone checks.

The iteration and human-feedback sequence is transcribed from the supplied development conversation. The later UI contract documents the result, rather than independently recording those requests. The selected images show the shipped panes; no image of the first expansion was recovered.
human: Bryan’s development conversation, supplied as context for this review, records the Share request and acceptance, followed by the request to apply the same interaction to Publish with its own icon. Original turn dates are unavailable. The release contract corroborates the resulting design.
followUp: The pane pattern is established. Later changes should preserve the compact controls and keep Share link and Publish to profile understandable as separate actions.
